clauses.reason: The order commands "do order that the said code of fair competition be and is hereby approved" for the Code of Fair Competition for the Laundry and Dry Cleaning Machinery Manufacturing Industry under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act; the approval has legal effect only through section 3 of that title (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so the prospective operative effect of this approval ended on June 14, 1935, the date of approval, because the resolution states no later effective date. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and the order states no own-terms end. June 16, 1935 is not an end, since section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The Schechter decision of May 27, 1935 is recorded only as a validity characterization, not an end date.

research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6314 is a one-command order: after reciting the application, hearings and the Administrator's findings under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, the President wrote "do order that the said code of fair competition be and is hereby approved" for the Code of Fair Competition for the Laundry and Dry Cleaning Machinery Manufacturing Industry. It states no period, condition, "until" date, provisional approval or exception, so no own-terms end applies. The command depends wholly on section 3 of Title I. Under the reviewed shared analysis, the first end of such a command is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935) unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held for this code.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued, and the section 5 exemption for action completed while the code was in effect is likewise an accrued effect (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5). Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after the repeal.
